title: Command palettes
description: A command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K) lists every action in the app, searchable by name: the discoverability solution for keyboard-first users. Every command is registered with a title, shortcut, and handler; the palette filters as you type and runs on Enter. It turns 'where is that menu item?' into three keystrokes.
mechanism: Command registry: (id, title, shortcut, handler, when-clause). Palette: input -> fuzzy filter -> list -> execute. When-clauses hide irrelevant commands per context.
algo: O(commands) filter per keystroke; fuzzy match O(pattern x title).

title: Fuzzy command matching
description: Command palettes match fuzzily — 'sav' finds 'File: Save', 'fsv' too — because users remember fragments, not titles. The scorer rewards word-boundary and prefix matches, consecutive runs, and short gaps; it penalizes scattered matches. The same algorithms as fuzzy file finders apply, tuned for short command titles instead of paths.
mechanism: Subsequence match with bonuses (boundary, camelCase, consecutive) and gap penalties; rank by score; show the top ~10. Precompute lowercase titles; match per keystroke.
algo: O(pattern x title) per command; top-k heap for large registries.

title: Keyboard-first UX
description: Keyboard-first design means every action is reachable without the mouse: shortcuts for the frequent, the palette for the rest, and visible hints everywhere. The design rules are consistency (same keys do the same things), discoverability (shortcuts shown in menus and the palette), and escape hatches (Esc always backs out). Mouse users lose nothing; keyboard users gain everything.
mechanism: Shortcut map (no conflicts, checked at build); palette for the long tail; focus management so keyboard state is always visible. Test with keyboard only — no mouse allowed.
algo: Design discipline; conflict detection O(shortcuts^2) at build.

title: Command registry
description: The command registry is the app's action catalog: every command registered once with id, title, icon, shortcut, precondition, and handler. Menus, palettes, toolbars, and keyboard shortcuts are all views over the registry — add a command once, it appears everywhere consistently. Preconditions (when-clauses) control visibility per context.
mechanism: Register at startup/plugin load; views subscribe to registry changes. Execute by id; the registry resolves the handler. Preconditions evaluated per context (editor focus, selection).
algo: O(1) execute by id; O(commands) to render a view.

title: Context-aware commands
description: The palette shows different commands per context: with text selected, 'sort lines' appears; in a test file, 'run test' jumps to the top. Context-awareness comes from when-clauses evaluated against the current state (selection, file type, cursor position). It keeps the palette short and relevant instead of an overwhelming phone book.
mechanism: Context keys (editorHasSelection, resourceExtname, inTestFile...); when-clauses as boolean expressions; re-evaluate on context change. Rank context-matching commands higher.
algo: O(commands) filter per context change; expressions are tiny.
demo:
cmds = [
    ('sort-lines', lambda c: c.get('selection')),
    ('run-test', lambda c: c.get('file', '').endswith('_test.py')),
    ('save', lambda c: True),
]

for ctx in ({'selection': True, 'file': 'a.py'}, {'file': 'a_test.py'}, {'file': 'a.py'}):
    visible = [name for name, when in cmds if when(ctx)]
    print('%-42s -> %s' % (ctx, visible))
print('when-clauses keep the palette short and relevant per context')

title: Recent commands
description: Recent-commands tracking surfaces what you actually use: the palette's default view (empty query) lists your most recent and frequent commands. It is personalization with zero configuration — the app learns your workflow from usage. Recency-weighted frequency (like the completion ranker) keeps it fresh as habits change.
mechanism: Log command executions with timestamps; score = recency decay x frequency; empty-query palette shows top-N. Per-user, on-device.
algo: O(1) log per execution; O(commands log commands) to rank on palette open.
demo:
import time
log = []
NOW = 1000

def run(cmd):
    log.append((cmd, NOW - len(log)))  # simulated timestamps

for c in ['save', 'find', 'save', 'palette', 'save', 'find']:
    run(c)

from collections import Counter
freq = Counter(c for c, _ in log)
recent = {}
for cmd, ts in log:
    recent[cmd] = max(recent.get(cmd, 0), 0.9 ** (NOW - ts))
ranked = sorted(freq, key=lambda c: freq[c] * recent[c], reverse=True)
print('empty-query palette (your top commands):', ranked)
print('zero configuration: the app learns your workflow from usage')

title: Plugin commands
description: Plugins extend the palette: each plugin registers its commands into the shared registry with a namespace prefix ('Git: ...', 'Docker: ...'). The host handles filtering, ranking, and execution uniformly — plugins just declare. Sandboxing keeps a misbehaving plugin from freezing the palette; lazy loading keeps startup fast.
mechanism: Plugin manifest declares commands; host loads handlers on first use (lazy); namespaced titles avoid collisions. Permissions per plugin (which commands it may contribute).
algo: O(plugins) registration; lazy load keeps startup O(core).

title: Natural language commands
description: Natural-language commands let users type 'make the text bigger' instead of hunting for 'View: Increase Font Size'. An intent classifier (or LLM) maps the utterance to a command id with arguments; low-confidence maps fall back to fuzzy title matching. It is the palette's friendly front door — imprecise, forgiving, and surprisingly effective for the long tail of rarely-used commands.
mechanism: Intent model: utterance -> (command, args, confidence). Confidence < threshold -> show fuzzy matches instead. Log corrections to improve the mapping.
algo: O(1) model call or O(commands) embedding match. Fallback keeps it safe.
demo:
# intent map: utterances -> (command, args); fallback to fuzzy titles
INTENTS = [
    (('bigger', 'larger', 'zoom in'), ('view.zoomIn', {})),
    (('save',), ('file.save', {})),
    (('dark', 'theme'), ('view.themeDark', {})),
]

def nl(query):
    words = set(query.lower().split())
    best, bs = None, 0
    for keys, cmd in INTENTS:
        s = len(words & set(keys))
        if s > bs:
            best, bs = cmd, s
    return best if bs else None

for q in ('make the text bigger', 'save this', 'switch to dark theme', 'do a barrel roll'):
    hit = nl(q)
    print('%-24r -> %s' % (q, hit[0] if hit else 'no intent: fall back to fuzzy title match'))

title: Command telemetry
description: Command telemetry measures what the palette is for: which commands run, how long filtering takes, and where users give up (typed but didn't run). The metrics drive ranking (popular commands first), performance (p99 filter latency), and pruning (commands nobody runs are candidates for removal). Privacy: aggregate counts, never keystroke contents.
mechanism: Log (command id, latency, abandoned queries as hashes); aggregate; dashboards per command. Never log query text — only that a query happened and whether it led to execution.
demo:
from collections import Counter
# (command, filter_ms, executed?) -- query TEXT never logged
telemetry = [
    ('file.save', 12, True), ('edit.find', 8, True), ('view.zoom', 45, False),
    ('file.save', 10, True), ('git.commit', 60, False),
]
uses = Counter(c for c, _, e in telemetry if e)
abandoned = [c for c, ms, e in telemetry if not e]
print('executions:', dict(uses))
print('abandoned after typing:', abandoned, '(ranking or naming problem?)')
print('p99 filter latency: %dms (budget: <50ms)' % max(ms for _, ms, _ in telemetry))

title: Accessibility of palettes
description: Command palettes must work for everyone: full keyboard operation (obviously), screen-reader announcements (results count, selected item), sufficient contrast, and no keyboard traps. The palette is often the most accessible part of an app — one input, one list — which makes it the accessibility fallback for pointer-heavy features. Test with a screen reader, not just a keyboard.
mechanism: ARIA listbox semantics; live region announces result counts; visible focus; Esc closes and returns focus. Every palette action also available without the palette (menus).
algo: O(1) semantics work; the testing is the cost.

title: Theming command UI
description: The palette is UI and must theme: colors from the theme tokens (not hardcoded), density options, and font scaling. Since it overlays everything, it also needs backdrop treatment (dim/blur) that respects reduced-transparency settings. Theming is token-driven — the palette reads the same tokens as the rest of the app, so custom themes just work.
mechanism: Theme tokens for all colors/spacing; respect prefers-reduced-transparency; density setting. No hardcoded colors in palette code — ever.

title: Palette performance
description: The palette must filter in under 16ms per keystroke or typing feels laggy: precompute lowercase titles, match with early exit, cap the rendered list (virtualize beyond ~50), and debounce expensive rankers. Large registries (10k+ commands with plugins) need indexed matching — trigram prefilter then fuzzy on candidates. Profile with the real registry, not a toy one.
mechanism: Precompute; early-exit matching; virtualized list; debounce rankers; trigram prefilter for huge registries. Budget: 16ms/keystroke.
algo: Precompute, early-exit matching, virtualized lists, debounced rankers; budget enforced per keystroke.
demo:
import time, random
random.seed(1)

titles = ['Command %d action' % i for i in range(20000)]
lower = [t.lower() for t in titles]  # precomputed once

def filt(q):
    q = q.lower()
    return [t for t, l in zip(titles, lower) if q in l][:50]  # cap rendered

t = time.perf_counter()
res = filt('action 199')
dt = (time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000
print('20k commands filtered in %.1fms -> %d shown (virtualize the rest)' % (dt, len(res)))
print('budget 16ms/keystroke: precompute, early-exit, cap, virtualize')

title: Discoverability
description: The palette's job is discoverability, but users must discover the palette: the shortcut in the menu, the hint on empty states, the onboarding nudge ('press Ctrl+K'). In-app command search (help menu) routes to the palette. The metric is palette adoption — what fraction of actions run through it — and it grows with every hint placed where users already look.
mechanism: Hints in menus (show the shortcut), empty-state nudges, onboarding tour, help-menu search. Measure adoption; place hints where users look.

title: Multi-modal command input
description: Commands accept more than typed text: voice ('save the file'), gesture, and recent-context ('do that again'). The input layer normalizes to (command, args) regardless of modality; the registry does not care how the command was invoked. Voice needs confirmation UX (show what was heard, confirm destructive actions); gestures need discoverability even more than keys.
mechanism: Modality adapters -> normalized (command, args, confidence). Confirmation for destructive/irreversible. Same registry, same telemetry, per-modality UX.

title: Testing command systems
description: Command systems need tests at three levels: registry integrity (no duplicate ids, no shortcut conflicts, all handlers callable), matching quality (golden queries -> expected top result), and end-to-end (invoke via palette, assert the effect). Shortcut conflicts are build failures; matching regressions are caught by the golden set. Fuzz the parser with random inputs — it must never crash.
mechanism: Build-time checks (conflicts, duplicates); golden query set in CI; e2e palette tests. Fuzz inputs for crash-safety.
